Conflict classes seen: exactly ONE — import-block widening (known 2026-08-31 class) in `lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/pipeline/finalize.rs`: our `crate::context::keys` vs upstream's new `crate::billing_rollup` re-export (billing-rollup types moved to `fabro-types`); kept both, both provably used. Merge committed as `c3d59ab44` on `fabro/run/01M1SR27KEJGNQ1HFN9266ZCZE`; report at `.fabro/reports/merge-upstream/5d290a609.md`. No seeds superseded; fabro-b7c4 upstream PR offer still valid.
data.painpoints: 1) The merge node's `fs_write=""` blocked file-tool edits even for conflict resolution and the report — had to route all writes through the shell (documented escape hatch); worth an explicit glob or a policy note in `.fabro/workflows/merge-upstream/workflow.fabro`. 2) `scripts/qualitygate.nu` silently degrades to fmt+check-only when the merge bumps root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` (always true for upstream merges), so the 'expect near-full fmt+clippy+nextest' contract required a manual supplemental run of clippy+nextest on the merge-touched crates — consider a merge-mode flag on the gate. 3) Two environmental flakes cost ~20min of reruns: the documented fabro-80b3 timeout class plus `pull_request_creation_persists_generation_failure` failing once under 5-crate load (helpers untouched by the merge; green in 3 subsequent runs). 4) `mise trust` was required before `just` recipes would run in this sandbox. 5) First cold `cargo build --workspace` exceeded the 600s default tool timeout — merges need explicit `timeout_ms` headroom.
